acceptance: The owner's choice of signal is recorded in context before implementation starts.
A run whose refresh outcome is conflict or failed produces that signal while still opening or updating the keyed issue exactly as today.
Later runs that skip the unchanged failed input behave as the chosen option specifies, without re-raising or duplicating the issue.
MAINTAINING.md (Issues section) describes the signal, and controller tests cover a conflict run, a skipped-unchanged run, a retry dispatch and a workflow_run nudge.
context:
Purpose: lowers the risk that the next upstream release stops on a conflict, which would fail the core item sqlglot-e2e-first-release-certification (BenchBox-dev/BenchBox tracker; cross-tracker needs are not possible).

Decision gate (owner, before implementation): choose one: (a) only the run that first records the conflict fails (one notification, then quiet); (b) every scheduled run fails while the issue is open (persistent, noisy, also red on workflow_run nudges unless excluded); (c) runs stay green and the issue gets a label or a commit status that an alert watches. Record the choice here.

Verification rubric: (1) new controller tests fail before and pass after; (2) existing controller and contract tests pass; (3) a dry-run dispatch against a deliberately conflicting fixture or recorded plan shows the chosen signal; (4) the outcome table in MAINTAINING.md matches the code.

Guardrails: no change to issue keying, dedupe, skip-unchanged logic or the publish job's mutation rules; a failing signal must not let publish run or skip readiness; prepare-failed, publish-refused and publish-failed keep their current non-zero exits; no new permission or secret.

Owner decision 2026-11-14 (choice dialog): option (a): the run that first raises or changes a conflict/failed issue fails; runs that skip the unchanged input stay green; the same rule applies to drift issues.
description: When downstream.refresh auto exits with status conflict or failed, the controller opens issue-only escalation and the workflow run still concludes success. The v30.31.0 conflict (issue #88, run 43024772570) showed as a green run on 2026-11-11, and the next scheduled runs skipped the unchanged input and were green too; it was noticed only by comparing versions by hand. prepare-failed, publish-refused and publish-failed already exit non-zero (MAINTAINING.md, Issues), so the refresh-stopped outcomes are the quiet exception.
